subject: Re: Redwood sizing questions — latency & throughput targets (Finex)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@finexpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 14:32:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — latency/throughput sizing (Finex)

Thanks again for a productive call earlier today — appreciated the clarity on your payment-routing workload.

Quick recap of the performance constraints you shared and our action items:

- Latency SLO: 95th percentile under 120ms for single-request streaming responses (user-facing confirmations).
- Throughput: steady-state 180 QPS for small-chat endpoints (~80 tokens/response平均), peak bursts up to 600 QPS during promo spikes.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent-heavy windows of ~1,200 concurrent open streams during peak; steady-state concurrency ~400.
- Tokens/sec target: baseline aggregate ~14k tokens/sec steady, peaks up to ~48k tokens/sec for 90s promo bursts.
- Streaming: need support for chunked token streaming (first token within 30ms, continued streaming at <=10ms per chunk).

Action items I committed to:
1) Share a preliminary throughput-sizing worksheet with token/QPS conversions and recommended instance classes (attached: redwood-sizing-sheet.xlsx).
2) Validate whether your internal routing layer performs request coalescing — you mentioned edge-level dedup; Aditya to follow up with routing-specific questions.
3) Recommend canary plan: start with a 20% traffic test on Redwood Dedicated with autoscale headroom for bursts.

Please review the attached sizing sheet and the prod profile you offered to export. If these numbers look right, we'll run a quick internal capacity estimate and share a proposed Dedicated reservation and fallback model.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: redwood-sizing-sheet.xlsx

From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@finexpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:05:18 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — latency/throughput sizing (Finex)

Thanks Marissa — that recap is perfect. A couple of clarifications from our side:

1) The 95th percentile 120ms target is for the full end-to-end path (edge + model). We currently see ~40–60ms at our edge for small payloads, so you should assume ~60–80ms available for the model stack.
2) Token assumptions: our avg confirmation responses are around 80 tokens, but we do have larger investigator flows that can be 350–500 tokens — those are <1% of traffic but important for UX.
3) For streaming: first-byte is critical. We need the first token to arrive within 20–30ms for the confirmation flow; subsequent streaming can be relaxed.

I've attached the prod profile export (finex-prod-profile.csv) — it includes hour-of-day QPS and token distributions. Let me know if you need a different format.

We'll loop in our infra lead (Maya Torres) on the capacity conversation — she prefers to see instance-level recommendations and cost estimates.

Cheers,
Rajiv
Rajiv Shah
Director, Engineering
Finex Payments
rajiv.shah@finexpay.com

Attachments: finex-prod-profile.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@finexpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — latency/throughput sizing (Finex)

Perfect — thanks for the prod profile. Quick notes after a first pass on the CSV:

- Peak shaping: your peak windows are very short (60–120s) but very sharp — this favors autoscaling + burst capacity vs large reserved headroom.
- Token distribution: the 99th token-size bucket is dominated by the investigator flows (350–500 tokens). We'll model those as 'long tail' and propose separate routing to non-blocking model variants.
- Suggested instance classes: for the steady-state 14k tokens/sec we recommend 6xA100-like serving replicas (quantized FP16) with autoscale to 20 during peaks; for the long-tail 500-token requests, we recommend a dedicated small-pool of CPU-backed workers or offload to multi-chunk mode to avoid blocking short confirmations.

Next steps:
- Aditya will run a quick benchmark using your CSV to provide tokens/sec => GPU count mapping and expected p95 latency. Expect his note Monday AM.
- We'll draft a mutual action plan and a 2-week canary runbook (traffic split, observability checks, fallback).

I'll create a shared Drive folder with the runbook and cost/instance estimates; sending link shortly.

— Marissa

From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv.shah@finexpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Torres <maya@finexpay.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:12:10 -0800

Sounds good. We'll plan to kick off the canary the week of Mar 9. Maya will own the infra side and will expect a simple action list (instance types, expected cost range, monitoring thresholds for p95 and error-rate).

One question: for the streaming first-byte objective, what are realistic expectations for p50/p95 at the network hop to the model when using Redwood Dedicated in us-west-2?

Thanks,
